question: I need help with setting up two different emails on my website. One for receiving order invoices and the other for general inquiries. Im specifically looking for guidance on how to set the email address for order confirmations in the Business Info section of my sites settings.
candidate_answer:
To set up two different emails on your website—one for order invoices and another for general inquiries—and configure the order confirmation email in the Business Info section, follow these steps:

- **Create additional business email addresses** for your domain, such as orders@yourdomain.com and info@yourdomain.com. This requires purchasing additional business emails through your account [S1].
- To set up these emails:
  - Go to Business Email in your Wix account.
  - Click "Show User Info" on the relevant account.
  - Click the "More Actions" icon and select "Set Up User."
  - Sign in to your Google Workspace account.
  - Add new users with the desired email addresses (e.g., orders@yourdomain.com, info@yourdomain.com) [S1, S2].
- After creating the emails, **configure the order confirmation email address in the Business Info section** of your site settings by entering the orders@yourdomain.com email where order notifications are sent. (Note: Specific steps for this configuration in Business Info are not detailed in the retrieved context, but typically this is done in site settings under Business Info or Notifications.)
- Allow up to 24 hours for the new email accounts to become active [S2].

If you need detailed guidance on setting the order confirmation email specifically in the Business Info section, please check your site settings under Business Info or contact Wix support for exact navigation steps.

References: [S1], [S2]

question: I need to update the og:image for my entire site to ensure the correct image appears when the link is posted on social media. I also want to know if this will affect the image when the link is posted in an email or on Instagram.
candidate_answer:
To update the og:image for your entire site:

- Go to your site's settings in the Wix Editor.
- Click "Website settings."
- Scroll down to "General social image" and click "Upload Image."
- Select or upload the desired image, then click "Choose File" and save.
- Publish your site to apply changes [S1].

Regarding the impact on image display:

- The og:image primarily controls the thumbnail shown when your site link is shared on social media platforms like Facebook and X.
- For email clients, the image display depends on the email service and how it handles link previews; og:image may or may not be used consistently.
- Instagram does not generate link previews with og:image, so the image will not appear automatically when posting links there.

Therefore, updating the og:image ensures consistent social media sharing thumbnails but may not affect email or Instagram link previews [S1, S2].

question: Im experiencing trouble with the website editor. Theres a stray logo on the published version that doesnt show up in the editor, making it impossible to correct.
candidate_answer:
The issue of a stray logo appearing on the published website but not in the editor may be due to cached content or a discrepancy between the editor view and the live site. Here are steps to troubleshoot:

- Clear your browser cache or try viewing the site in an incognito/private window to rule out caching issues.
- Check if the logo is part of any hidden or conditional elements, such as repeaters or dynamic content connected via CMS, which might not be visible in the editor by default [S2].
- Review any Logo + Website plan settings, as logos purchased are digital goods and cannot be refunded or altered after download, meaning the logo might be embedded in the plan or template [S1].
- If the logo is part of a repeater or dynamic section, verify the repeater content and layout in Editor X to ensure no hidden items are causing the display [S2].

If these steps do not resolve the issue, contacting support with specific site details is recommended for further investigation.

question: Im unable to access the Google Maps element in the footer of my Wix site. Im having trouble removing it, and I dont know where the overlapping items feature is located.
candidate_answer:
To access and remove the Google Maps element in your Wix site's footer when it's difficult to select:

- Open the Layers panel in the Wix Editor by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of the editor. Navigate to the Footer section to locate the Google Maps element and select it directly from the list.
- Use the Overlapping Items feature by right-clicking on the element that is covering the Google Maps element. Then hover over "Overlapping Items" in the context menu and select the Google Maps element from the submenu.
- If the Overlapping Items feature does not work, right-click the covering element, hover over "Arrange," and select "Move Backward" repeatedly until the Google Maps element becomes accessible.
- Alternatively, use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + M (Cmd + Shift + M on Mac) to toggle through the elements on the page until the Google Maps element is selected.

These steps will help you locate and remove the Google Maps element even if it is hidden behind other elements or outside the gridlines [S1][S2].
